analysis:
Reviewed scripts/test-provider-ci-workflow.py (base text lines 1-868 only; the head side and most of the diff are not supplied). It is an offline unittest that asserts structure of CI workflows (provider-tests.yml, ci-master.yml, provider-plan.yml, action.yml). It is not shipped provider/runtime code, so no threat-model asset (A-001..A-020) or trust boundary (TB-002/003/007/011/012) is directly touched by the visible content.

The patch excerpt shows the test's VALIDATE_GIT constant being hardened. A restored .git cache is now rejected if it is a symlink, holds symlinks, holds non-sample hooks, or its config sets core.fsmonitor, core.hooksPath or includes. It also adds a CACHE_GATE_STEP for Darkbloom Sandbox runners without a Darkbloom cache. These are CI supply-chain hardening changes and strengthen rather than weaken controls. The excerpt is truncated, so the actual workflow YAML implementing them and the remaining test assertions were not visible.

I examined the base-side assertions on cache save policy (SAVE_CACHES limited to push to master/dev and dev dispatch), pinned action SHAs, fail-closed gates, and PRs never saving caches; none are shown being relaxed in the visible range. Remaining question for integration: whether the workflow files (provider-tests.yml, provider-plan.yml, the actions) match the new test assertions. I could not verify that the hook/config scan avoids executing restored git config, though `git config --file` only parses. Residual checks such as `find -exec git config --file` on untrusted content were not evaluated against head text.
